newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Canadian Mountie ends Indonesia visit over Busang.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Mountie ends Indonesia visit over Busang.

text.p: An officer from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) on Tuesday ended a four-day visit to Indonesia to discuss investigations into the Busang gold scandal.

Douglas Herda, senior RCMP liaison officer for Southeast Asia, declined to comment on the outcome of his trip, which came on the heels of the collapse of the Busang project in East Kalimantan province.
The Busang discovery was touted by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd as the largest gold find of the century but independent tests showed it contained virtually no gold.
"I cannot comment on anything. Any information will have to come from Canada," he told Reuters before leaving for Singapore, where he is based.

The Suara Pembaruan newspaper reported on Tuesday that a Singapore-based Canadian police officer had visited Bre-X's warehouse in the East Kalimantan capital of Samarinda where the company's core samples were stored.
The afternoon newspaper quoted an unidentified employee at the warehouse as saying the officer and a local policeman checked documents at the warehouse. It did not identify Herda.
Consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd said in its audit report on Busang that Bre-X's storage warehouse in Samarinda was the most likely place for any tampering with core samples.
Brigadier-General Ahwil Luthan, secretary of the National Central Bureau which handles investigations requiring Interpol assistance, denied Herda had visited Samarinda.
"He was just in Jakarta," he told Reuters. "He didn't go there," he said, when asked to comment on the newspaper report.
The Busang project, in which the Indonesian government held a 10 percent stake, collapsed after Strathcona said it found no economic gold deposit on the property.
Strathcona also said Bre-X data on the Busang discovery was falsified on an unprecedented scale.
Indonesian and Canadian police are investigating the scandal -- the biggest mining fraud in history.
